assignment:
Some of your friends perform community service. For example, some tutor elementary school children and others clean up litter. They think helping the community is very important. But other friends of yours think community service takes too much time away from what they need or want to do. 
Your principal is deciding whether to require all students to perform community service. 
Write a letter to your principal in which you take a position on whether students should be required to perform community service. Support your position with examples.
essay_1:
Dear Principal,

I am writing about if students should have to do community service. I think every student should have to do it, but only if the hours arent crazy and we get to pick what we do.

First, community service teaches you stuff you cant learn in class. My friend Maya tutors second graders at Lincoln Elementary two times a week. She said teaching fractions to a little kid made her actually understand them better. She also learned to be patient with the kids who get mad when they dont get it. You need stuff like that for pretty much any job when your older.

Second, it makes you care more about where you live. Last spring me and my friends picked up trash by the creek behind the park. We filled like twenty bags in one afternoon. Now when I walk by the creek and I see trash I pick it up. Honestly I never cared about that place until we cleaned it.

I know some kids are going to say they are already to busy with homework and sports and stuff, and some of them have jobs. Thats true and its fair. But if it was only like twenty hours a year, thats not even half an hour a week. Plus the school could count stuff kids already do, like coaching a little kids team or helping with a food drive at church. That way it wouldnt feel like extra work.

Making community service required would help our town and it would make us better people. Please think about making it something you have to do to graduate from our school.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
essay_2:
Dear Principal,

I am writing about whether our school should make community service required. I think every student should have to do it, as long as the hours are reasonable and students get to pick how they help.

First, community service teaches things you can't learn in a classroom. My friend Maya tutors second graders at Lincoln Elementary two times a week. She told me that explaining fractions to a seven year old made her understand them better herself. She also learned patience and how to talk to kids who get upset. She will use those skills at any job later.

Second, service connects students to the town they live in. Last spring a group of us picked up trash along the creek behind the park. It was hard and dirty, but we had a great time doing it together. We filled twenty bags in one afternoon. Now when I walk by that creek, I notice when trash shows up and I pick it up. I didn't care about that spot before we worked on it.

I know some students say they are already busy with homework, sports, and jobs. That is fair. But twenty hours a year is less than half an hour a week, and that is not much. The school could also count things students already do, like coaching a little league team or helping at a church food drive. That way it would feel normal instead of like extra work.

Requiring service would help our town and help students grow. Please think about making it part of graduating from our school.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
